name: Ana West
life: “I still remember carrying water for someone who couldn't put the phone down.” People around Maré Coffee know Ana by a small Wednesday habit. Ana likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I walked over with a cup of water. I am grateful the letter didn't mention me because I cried afterward.
appearance: Ana has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Look for a center part and straight chestnut hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a plum-colored cardigan with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. In conversation Ana listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Ana thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Ana sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To ask the coworker for an ordinary lunch after the call.
family: Paul Smith is Ana’s half-sibling. Ana knows which ones can be shared. Paul keeps the photographs. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *The misplaced umbrella*, Paul says, “I saw the switch but the toddler holding both had just learned mine and yours.”
connections: Ravi Stone. Bringing water into a quiet room was the part both can discuss without disclosing the call.
